There's a Global Network of Fungi Under Your Feet. This Is the First Complete Map

2026-07-05 Marta Musso, WIRED mycorrhizal network, global mapping, fungal filaments, underground ecosystem, Science journal, plant-fungal symbiosis, spatial ecology
Read the source article

Quick summary

An international research team has produced the first global map of the vast underground mycorrhizal fungal network, revealing a system of symbiotic fungal filaments stretching an estimated 110 quadrillion kilometers worldwide.

Key takeaways

  • First-ever global map of underground mycorrhizal fungal networks published in the journal Science
  • The network of fungal filaments stretches an estimated 110 quadrillion kilometers — nearly a billion times the Earth-Sun distance
  • Mycorrhizal fungi form mutually beneficial partnerships with plant roots across the planet, supporting terrestrial ecosystems
  • The mapping combines field sampling, ecological modeling, and global geospatial data to predict fungal distribution
  • Understanding fungal network distribution is critical for climate regulation, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem health
  • The map reveals how underground microbial geography varies with climate, soil, and vegetation patterns globally
